1(a).assumed: Gradient of a v–t graph is acceleration; negative gradient means deceleration; straight line means constant.

1(b).assumed: Displacement is the area under a v–t graph (triangle area ½ × base × height).

2.assumed: Motor lifts known mass a measured height; electrical input VIt, useful output mgh; efficiency ratio; safety with falling masses.

3(a).assumed: Metre rule for height; electronic timing started by electromagnet release or light gate and stopped by trapdoor or second gate.

3(b).assumed: Square the time, matching the table's significant figures.

3(c)(i).assumed: Plot the point accurately and draw a straight best-fit line.

3(c)(ii).assumed: Gradient from a large triangle on the best-fit line.

3(d)(i).assumed: Use s = ut + ½at² with u = 0 and a = g, then rearrange for t².

3(d)(ii).assumed: Gradient of t² against h equals 2/g, so g = 2/gradient.

4(a).assumed: Weight of a uniform plank acts at its centre; moment uses perpendicular component T sin θ of the cable tension.

4(b).assumed: Combine stress F/A and strain x/L in E = stress/strain; rearrange for extension.

5(a).assumed: Statement: resultant force is proportional to (equals) rate of change of momentum.

5(b)(ii).assumed: Impulse is area under F–t graph and equals Δp; momentum reverses sign on rebound.

5(b)(iii).assumed: In an elastic collision kinetic energy is conserved; lower rebound speed means KE was lost.

6(a).assumed: Filament lamp has a curved I–V graph; an ohmic resistor gives a straight line through the origin.

6(b).assumed: Parallel currents add; lost volts = e.m.f. − terminal p.d.; r = lost volts ÷ current.

6(c)(i).assumed: Use a micrometer; repeat at different places and orientations and average.

6(c)(ii).assumed: Area of one strand πd²/4; parallel strands give total area of all strands; ρ = RA/L.

6(c)(iii).assumed: Add percentage uncertainties, doubling the diameter's because area depends on d².

7(a).assumed: Incident and reflected waves superpose to form a stationary wave; maximum-to-minimum spacing is λ/4; f = c/λ.

7(b).assumed: Microwaves are transverse and plane polarised; the grille blocks them when rods align with the oscillations, passes them at 90°.

8(a)(i).assumed: Refractive index n = c/v; rearrange for speed or index.

8(a)(ii).assumed: Frequency is unchanged, so wavelength in a medium = wavelength in air ÷ n.

8(b)(i).assumed: Snell's law n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ with air n = 1.

8(b)(ii).assumed: Entering higher index bends towards the normal; lower index bends away; with n sin θ constant the final angle is below 37°.

9(a)(i).assumed: hf is the energy of one photon.

9(a)(ii).assumed: Work function is the minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the metal surface.

9(b)(i).assumed: Convert φ to joules; KEmax = hf − φ; v = √(2KE/m).

9(b)(ii).assumed: Photon energy depends only on frequency; intensity changes photon number, so maximum speed is unchanged.
